name: TITAN 2
question: Does the Medtronic implantable tibial neuromodulation system achieve a six-month urgency urinary incontinence responder rate above a 40% performance goal?

design.population: 126 implanted adults with urgency urinary incontinence after failure or intolerance of at least two overactive bladder medications at US sites.
design.description: Prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm pivotal device study
design.locator: Methods, Study Design; Results, Subject Enrollment and Demographics

verdictNote: Six-month responder rate exceeded the 40% performance goal in a single-arm study.
takeaway: In the single-arm TITAN 2 study of the Medtronic leadless rechargeable tibial neurostimulator, 59% of participants with six-month diary data had at least 50% fewer urgency incontinence episodes, exceeding the prespecified 40% goal; the all-implanted analysis reported 61% at 12 months.

reports.label: Six- and 12-month pivotal report
reports.citation: Lee U, Xavier K, Carey J, et al. "Implantable Tibial Neuromodulation Therapy Improves Symptoms of Urge Urinary Incontinence From the TITAN 2 Pivotal Study." *J Urol.* 2026;215(6):702-712. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000004958
reports.followUp: Primary outcome at 6 months; safety and observed or imputed efficacy through 12 months
reports.followUpLocator: Methods, Study Design and Statistical Analysis; Results, UUI and Safety

results.measure: At least 50% fewer daily UUI episodes on a 3-day diary at 6 months among complete cases; prespecified performance goal 40%
results.note: One-sided alpha 0.025. Missing data did not exceed the prespecified 5% threshold for imputation at 6 months.
results.locator: Methods, Statistical Analysis; Results, UUI; Figure 3

results.measure: At least 50% fewer daily UUI episodes at 12 months; all implanted with imputation
results.note: Missing data exceeded 5% at 12 months, triggering the prespecified imputation approach.
results.locator: Methods, Statistical Analysis; Results, UUI; Figure 3

results.measure: No UUI episodes on the follow-up diary at 6 and 12 months
results.note: The article reports 95% CIs of 12%-27% and 15%-31%, respectively.
results.locator: Results, UUI; Supplementary Figure 1 cited therein

results.measure: Mean daily voids among subjects with baseline frequency of at least 10 voids/day, baseline to 6 months
Mean increase from baseline at 6 months
Mean improvement from baseline at 6 and 12 months

values.exp: 27.1 points (95% CI 22.6-31.7) at 6 months; 25.5 points (95% CI 20.7-30.3) at 12 months

results.note: Six-month P value applies to the prespecified change from baseline.

harms.label: Adverse device effects through 12 months
harms.note: Related to device, procedure, therapy or study aids; 10 participants had grade 1 and 17 had grade 2 events, with overlap between grades.

harms.label: Procedure-related implant-site infection
harms.note: Article text reports 7%; Table 3 lists implant infection in 5, incision cellulitis in 3, and wound infection in 1. These categories may overlap. Other infections resolved with antibiotics.

harms.label: Serious adverse device effect
harms.note: Resolved Clostridium difficile colitis possibly related to perioperative antibiotics. FDA additionally classified the wound infection requiring explant as serious (P240011B, p33).

delivery.label: Enrollment and follow-up
delivery.value: 188 enrolled at 26 sites; 126 implanted; 125 completed 6 months; 118 completed 12 months
delivery.locator: Results, Subject Enrollment and Demographics; Figure 2

delivery.label: Preimplant testing
delivery.value: No evaluation stimulation period or prior percutaneous tibial neuromodulation required

delivery.label: Implant location and landmarks
delivery.value: Local anesthetic; subcutaneous pocket superficial to deep fascia over the tibial nerve. Mark 4 cm proximal to the medial malleolar midpoint and three-quarters of the way from tibia to Achilles; incision and insertion point 5 cm proximal to that mark. Suture loop permits repositioning; shallow fascial fixation optional.

delivery.label: Intraoperative response
delivery.value: 126/126 demonstrated a motor or sensory response during implantation

delivery.label: Implant setting
delivery.value: 36/126 hospital operating room; 44/126 ambulatory surgical center; 46/126 outpatient clinic procedure room

delivery.label: Stimulation schedule
delivery.value: 30 minutes every other day, 20 Hz, 200 microseconds pulse width, comfortable amplitude; therapy start within 24 hours

delivery.label: Study-device charging
delivery.value: Weekly charging recommended for the investigational device; article states commercial device typically needs annual or biannual charging

relations.note: TITAN 2 adopted the 40% responder performance goal used in the eCoin pivotal study.
